title: Piper PA-28 Cherokee (Archer, Warrior)

sources.title: JoyPro function tables MSFS2020/2024 and X-Plane 11/12 (DB/Functions)

intro: The Piper PA-28 Cherokee is a small four-seat plane with a low wing and one piston engine. It has one door on the right side. Each front seat has a control wheel. The engine levers are in a quadrant in the lower centre panel, and the trim wheel and the flap handle are on the floor between the seats.

areas.name: Flight instruments
areas.text: The round dials in front of the pilot.

panels.name: Flight instruments (the six-pack)
panels.text: The round dials in front of the pilot that show speed, tilt, height, turning, heading and climb. Together they are called the six-pack.
panels.context: The pilot looks at them to know how the plane flies, especially in clouds or at night.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane moves through the air.
controls.context: The pilot watches it on take-off and landing and to avoid flying too slowly.

controls.name: Attitude indicator (artificial horizon)
controls.text: This dial shows whether the nose is up or down and whether the wings are level, like a small model horizon.
controls.context: It is most useful when the real horizon cannot be seen.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows the height of the plane above sea level.
controls.context: The pilot sets the air-pressure value so that it reads correctly.

controls.name: Turn coordinator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane turns, and a ball shows whether the turn is smooth or the plane slides sideways.
controls.context: The pilot keeps the ball in the middle with the rudder pedals.

controls.name: Heading indicator
controls.text: This dial shows the compass direction the nose points to. It is driven by a gyro, a spinning wheel that keeps its direction.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to the magnetic compass from time to time.

controls.name: Vertical speed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane climbs or sinks.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to see whether the plane is holding its height.

controls.name: Tachometer
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the engine turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM).
controls.context: The engine speed tells the pilot how much power the engine gives.

areas.name: Radio stack
areas.text: The radios and navigators in the middle of the panel.

panels.name: Radio stack
panels.text: The radios and navigators in the middle of the panel, for talking to air traffic control and for navigating.
panels.context: The pilot tunes them before take-off and during the flight.

controls.name: Audio panel
controls.text: These buttons choose which radio the pilot talks on and listens to.
controls.context: It works like a switch box for the radios and the intercom.

controls.name: GPS / NAV / COM
controls.text: This unit combines a satellite navigator (GPS) with a navigation radio and a voice radio. A screen shows the frequencies and the route.
controls.context: The pilot enters the route and frequencies here.

controls.name: NAV / COM 2
controls.text: This is the second set of navigation and voice radio. Knobs set the frequencies, the station numbers.
controls.context: A second radio is a backup and lets the pilot hold two frequencies.

controls.name: Transponder
controls.text: The transponder answers radar so air traffic control can see the plane. The pilot sets a four-digit code, called the squawk.
controls.context: Air traffic control tells the pilot which code to set.

controls.name: Autopilot
controls.text: This optional autopilot panel holds the plane's wings level or its heading, and some versions also its height.
controls.context: It reduces the workload on long flights.

areas.name: Engine gauges
areas.text: The dials for the engine, fuel and electricity.

panels.name: Engine gauges
panels.text: The group of dials that show the health of the engine, the fuel and the electric system.
panels.context: The pilot checks them after starting the engine and from time to time during the flight.

controls.name: Fuel quantity gauges
controls.text: These dials show how much fuel is left in the left and right tank.
controls.context: The pilot keeps an eye on them so the plane does not run out of fuel.

controls.name: Oil temperature / pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature and the pressure of the engine oil.
controls.context: Oil keeps the engine parts from wearing out; the pilot checks it after starting.

controls.name: Fuel pressure gauge
controls.text: This dial shows the pressure of the fuel going to the engine.
controls.context: It tells the pilot that the fuel supply works.

controls.name: Ammeter / voltmeter
controls.text: This dial shows the electric current or the voltage of the electric system.
controls.context: It shows whether the alternator is charging the battery.

controls.name: EGT (exhaust gas temperature)
controls.text: This dial shows the temperature of the exhaust gases.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when leaning the mixture, which means reducing the fuel in the mixture.

areas.name: Lower panel and quadrant
areas.text: The lower centre panel with the engine levers, switches and the handles between the seats.

panels.name: Lower panel and throttle quadrant
panels.text: The lower centre panel with the engine levers, the electrical and fuel switches, the ignition key and the brake and flap handles.
panels.context: The pilot uses it for starting the engine, setting power and handling flaps and brakes.

controls.name: Throttle lever
controls.text: This lever sets how much power the engine gives. Pushing it forward gives more power.
controls.context: The pilot pushes it all the way for take-off.

controls.name: Mixture lever
controls.text: This red lever sets how much fuel is mixed with the air, from rich (more fuel) to idle cut-off, which stops the engine.
controls.context: The pilot makes the mixture leaner at higher altitudes, where the air is thinner.

controls.name: Carburettor heat lever

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: Cold air goes to the carburettor, the normal setting.

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Warm air goes to the carburettor to melt or prevent ice.

controls.text: Pulling this lever sends warmed air to the carburettor, the part that mixes fuel and air. This stops ice from forming in it.
controls.context: The pilot uses it where ice may form, and puts it off again for normal power.

controls.name: Master and alternator switches
controls.text: These switches connect the plane's electricity. The master switch connects the battery and the alternator makes power while the engine runs.
controls.context: They are used first when preparing the plane.

controls.name: Magneto / starter key

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The magnetos are off and the engine stops.

positions.name: BOTH
positions.text: Both magnetos work, the normal setting for flight.

positions.name: START
positions.text: The starter motor turns the engine; the key springs back.

controls.text: This key switches the magnetos on and starts the engine. Magnetos are small generators that make the sparks for the engine, and there are two for safety.
controls.context: The pilot turns it to BOTH after the engine runs and uses START to turn the engine over.

controls.name: Fuel pump and light switches
controls.text: These switches turn on the electric fuel pump, which helps to move fuel to the engine, and the lights outside the plane.
controls.context: The pilot uses the pump for the start, take-off and landing.

controls.name: Hand / parking brake lever
controls.text: This lever under the left panel sets the parking brake. The pilot pulls it and presses the button to hold it, with the toe brakes pressed.
controls.context: It is set when parked and released before taxiing.

controls.name: Flap handle

positions.text: Flaps are retracted for normal flight.
Flaps at 40 degrees, the most, for landing.

controls.text: This hand lever between the seats moves the flaps, parts of the wing which extend to give more lift at low speed. Pulling it up lowers the flaps by one notch; pressing the button lets it down.
controls.context: The flaps are used for take-off and landing.

controls.name: Stabilator trim wheel
controls.text: This wheel on the floor between the seats trims the nose up or down. The tail of this plane is a stabilator, a tail wing that moves as a whole. Trim removes the steady push on the controls.
controls.context: The pilot trims after changing speed.

controls.name: Fuel selector (left side wall)

positions.name: LEFT
positions.text: The left tank feeds the engine.

positions.name: RIGHT
positions.text: The right tank feeds the engine.

controls.text: This valve on the left side wall chooses which fuel tank feeds the engine, or turns the fuel off.
controls.context: The pilot changes tanks from time to time to keep the fuel balanced.

areas.name: Control wheel and pedals
areas.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.

panels.name: Control wheel and pedals
panels.text: The controls the pilot holds or pushes with the feet.
panels.context: Both front seats have a control wheel and pedals.

controls.name: Control wheel
controls.text: Pushing the wheel forward points the nose down, pulling it back points it up. Turning it rolls the plane left or right.
controls.context: The wheel moves the stabilator at the tail and the ailerons on the wings.

controls.name: Push-to-talk
controls.text: While this switch on the left horn of the wheel is pressed, the radio transmits.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to talk to air traffic control.

controls.name: Rudder pedals
controls.text: The pedals move the rudder on the tail to point the nose left or right. The tops of the pedals are the toe brakes for the left and right wheels.
controls.context: On the ground the brakes are used with the feet.
